mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month window indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages indicates robust consumer spending, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-2008 recovery regime, a monthly increase in the CPI index above 0.2 points signals the beginning of inflationary pressures, leading to expectations of monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.2 points during the post-2008 recovery, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production exceeding 1.0 percentage point over a 3-month period indicates a contraction in manufacturing and services, leading to lower corporate profits and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a quarterly GDP growth rate below 2.0% indicates an economic slowdown, prompting investors to reduce equity exposure and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 quarterly growth rate is below 2.0% during late-cycle expansions, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a robust labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is rising and UNRATE is falling, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
